sentences.en: Hello, welcome to The Rest is History, and I want to start today's episode by reading an index entry from a book called Seasons in the Sun, The Battle for Britain, 1974 to 1979.
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎收听《历史的余味》（The Rest is History）。今天这期节目，我想先读一本书的索引条目，书名是《阳光下的季节：1974至1979年英国之战》。

sentences.en: And in the index of this book, we find Thorpe, Jeremy, 1979 election, contracts gonorrhea from Greek prostitute, plans to have his ex-lover eaten by Florida alligators, scandal.
sentences.zh: 在这本书的索引里，我们发现了杰里米·索普（Jeremy Thorpe），1979年大选，从希腊妓女那里染上淋病，计划让前情人被佛罗里达的短吻鳄吃掉，丑闻。

sentences.en: Trial, wades ashore from sinking, hovercraft, and Wilson.
sentences.zh: 审判，从沉没的气垫船中涉水上岸，还有威尔逊。

sentences.en: And the man who compiled that index and wrote the book, Dominic Sandbrook, is, well, he's not sitting alongside me, he's in Chipping Norton and I'm in Brixton,
sentences.zh: 而编写那个索引并写下这本书的人，多米尼克·桑德布鲁克（Dominic Sandbrook），他——好吧，他没坐在我旁边，他在奇平诺顿，而我在布里克斯顿，

sentences.en: but he's virtually sitting alongside me.
sentences.zh: 但他几乎就像坐在我旁边一样。

sentences.en: Hello, Tom.
sentences.zh: 你好，汤姆。

sentences.en: The Jeremy Thorpe scandal.
sentences.zh: 杰里米·索普丑闻。

sentences.en: Now, this is a topic that lots of our British listeners will recognise because Hugh Grant and Ben Whishall were recently in a brilliant drama series about it,
sentences.zh: 这可是很多英国听众都会熟悉的话题，因为休·格兰特和本·卫肖最近主演了一部关于此事的精彩剧集，

sentences.en: a very British scandal.
sentences.zh: 《英国式丑闻》。

sentences.en: Those beyond Britain may not have the first idea what this is.
sentences.zh: 英国以外的人可能完全不知道这是什么。

sentences.en: So, we've got the questions written down here.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们把问题写在这里了。

sentences.en: Our most common question from all non-British listeners, what was the Jeremy Thorpe scandal?
sentences.zh: 我们从非英国听众那里收到的最常见的问题是：杰里米·索普丑闻到底是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good question.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是个好问题。

sentences.en: What was the Jeremy Thorpe scandal?
sentences.zh: 杰里米·索普丑闻是什么？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，非常感谢大家。

sentences.en: I love doing those indexes.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢做那些索引。

sentences.en: I'm glad you read that out.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你把它读了出来。

sentences.en: And we should say, shouldn't we, Tom, that this isn't our idea for the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而且我们应该说，汤姆，这不是我们自己想做的播客主题。

sentences.en: This is sent in by a listener, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是听众寄来的，对吧？

sentences.en: By Paul Keeley.
sentences.zh: 保罗·基利（Paul Keeley）寄来的。

sentences.en: By Paul Keeley.
sentences.zh: 是保罗·基利。

sentences.en: So, Paul, this one is for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，保罗，这一期是给你的。

sentences.en: And if nobody listens, it's all your fault.
sentences.zh: 如果没人听，那都是你的错。

sentences.en: So, what was the Jeremy Thorpe scandal?
sentences.zh: 那么，杰里米·索普丑闻是什么？

sentences.en: Well, that's basically what the podcast is about, so I won't give all the details away.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这基本上就是本期播客的内容，所以我不会把所有细节都剧透了。

sentences.en: But to cut a very long story short, Jeremy Thorpe was the leader of the Liberal Party in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 但长话短说，杰里米·索普是20世纪70年代自由党的领袖。

sentences.en: So, the Liberal Party was, as a regular listener of the podcast will know, it was one of the great, the two great parties of sort of British democracy in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 自由党，正如本播客的常客所知，它是19世纪英国民主政治的两大政党之一。

sentences.en: It had a pretty tough time and it declined.
sentences.zh: 它经历了一段相当艰难的时期，并走向了衰落。

sentences.en: But under Thorpe, it seemed to be making a bit of a comeback.
sentences.zh: 但在索普的领导下，它似乎有了复苏的迹象。

sentences.en: So, the Liberals were on almost 20% of the vote in February.
sentences.zh: 所以，自由党在2月份的得票率几乎达到了20%。

sentences.en: This is the 70s.
sentences.zh: 那是70年代。

sentences.en: Yeah, in February 1974.
And so, you know, you might say...
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，你可能会说……

sentences.en: That's the election where he was going around in a hovercraft.
sentences.zh: 那就是他坐着气垫船到处跑的那次选举。

sentences.en: No, it was in the next election, October 74.
sentences.zh: 不，那是下一次选举，1974年10月。

sentences.en: We'll come back to the hovercraft.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后再回过头来说气垫船的事。

sentences.en: So, Jeremy Thorpe is the leader of the Liberal Party.
sentences.zh: 所以，杰里米·索普是自由党领袖。

sentences.en: And as implausible as it may seem, his great sort of, you know, his ride to the top of British politics is interrupted.
sentences.zh: 尽管看起来不可思议，但他通往英国政治巅峰的道路却被打断了。

sentences.en: By the fact that he's accused of conspiring to murder his former lover, a stable hand and sometime model called Norman Scott.
sentences.zh: 原因是他被指控密谋杀害他的前情人，一个马夫兼业余模特，名叫诺曼·斯科特（Norman Scott）。

sentences.en: And at first, people think this story is completely mad.
sentences.zh: 起初，人们认为这个故事完全是疯了。

sentences.en: But then when they start looking into it, they see there's a bit more to it than that.
sentences.zh: 但当他们开始调查时，发现事情远不止于此。

sentences.en: And as the story unfolds, it brings in all these sort of bizarre characters.
sentences.zh: 随着故事的展开，它卷入了所有这些古怪的人物。

sentences.en: So, you've got a fruit machine dealer.
sentences.zh: 你有一个水果机经销商。

sentences.en: You've got a carpet salesman.
sentences.zh: 你有一个地毯推销员。

sentences.en: There's a plot, as you alluded to, to murder this man in Florida and feed him to alligators.
sentences.zh: 正如你提到的，还有一个在佛罗里达杀掉这个人并把他喂给短吻鳄的阴谋。

sentences.en: It sort of starts to suck in the Labour government.
sentences.zh: 它开始把工党政府也卷了进来。

sentences.en: The newspapers run it day after day after day.
sentences.zh: 报纸日复一日地报道它。

sentences.en: And it becomes this colossal kind of cause celebre in 70s Britain.
sentences.zh: 它成为了70年代英国轰动一时的事件。

sentences.en: It actually seems to, you know, a lot of questions are, well, why did it matter?
sentences.zh: 它似乎……你知道，很多问题都是，嗯，为什么这很重要？

sentences.en: I think one answer to that is it seemed to reflect a general sort of comic cedar-ness about British politics in the 70s and a sense of breakdown and so on.
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个答案是，它似乎反映了70年代英国政治中普遍存在的某种滑稽的颓废感，以及一种崩溃感等等。

sentences.en: And actually, you know, it happens at the same time as Watergate or a year or two after Watergate.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，你知道，它发生的时间和水门事件同时，或者在水门事件后一两年。

sentences.en: But it's a much more amusing story than Watergate.
sentences.zh: 但它比水门事件有趣得多。

sentences.en: And also, it is quite a tragic story, as you'll discover when we sort of go through it.
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你稍后会发现的，这也是一个相当悲剧的故事。

sentences.en: There's a lot of sort of broken lives involved amid all the sort of, you know, the sort of carnivalesque sort of bawdy farce.
sentences.zh: 在所有这些狂欢节般的粗俗闹剧之中，涉及了许多破碎的人生。

sentences.en: So, I mean, basically, so in the past, we've just done Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，过去我们讲的都是阿道夫·希特勒。

sentences.en: Yeah, Mohammed.
sentences.zh: 是的，穆罕默德。

sentences.en: We've done the origins of Islam.
sentences.zh: 我们讲过伊斯兰教的起源。

sentences.en: We've done the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 我们讲过法国大革命。

sentences.en: Vast, sweeping themes.
sentences.zh: 宏大、广阔的主题。

sentences.en: Here we're going up really up close to a subject that non-British listeners and even many British listeners will have never even heard of it.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们深入探讨了一个非英国听众，甚至许多英国听众可能从未听说过的主题。

sentences.en: And yet it is an absolutely brilliant story.
sentences.zh: 然而，这绝对是一个精彩的故事。

sentences.en: And as you say, it does kind of reveal all kinds of things about 1970s Britain.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它确实揭示了关于1970年代英国的各种事情。

sentences.en: But also, because it's about a gay affair.
sentences.zh: 但也因为它涉及一段同性恋情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is kind of midpoint between homosexuality having been criminalised in the 60s when Jeremy Thorpe is an up-and-coming young MP and is not worried about it being criminal.
sentences.zh: 这处于同性恋在60年代被定罪（当时杰里米·索普是一位崭露头角的年轻议员，并不担心它被定罪）和现在同性恋被完全接受的中间点。

sentences.en: I mean, he seems to have enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他似乎很享受。

sentences.en: He seems to have enjoyed the whiff of danger.
sentences.zh: 他似乎很享受那种危险的气息。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, of course, where we are now, where homosexuality is completely accepted.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有我们现在的处境，同性恋已被完全接受。

sentences.en: So it's also a kind of interesting temperature take on the course of that change as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这也是对这种变化过程的一个有趣的温度测量。

sentences.en: So I think in all kinds of ways, it well merits an episode.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为从各方面来看，它都值得做一期节目。

sentences.en: And I guess we should begin with Jeremy Thorpe himself.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该从杰里米·索普本人开始。

sentences.en: So we have a question from Stephen Clarke.
sentences.zh: 我们有一个来自斯蒂芬·克拉克（Stephen Clarke）的问题。

sentences.en: He's always sending us great questions.
sentences.zh: 他总是给我们发来很棒的问题。

sentences.en: And it says about Jeremy Thorpe, the son of a Conservative MP, an old Etonian, a Trinity College man, possessing an obsession with marrying Princess Margaret.
sentences.zh: 关于杰里米·索普，保守党议员之子，老伊顿生，三一学院毕业生，痴迷于娶玛格丽特公主。

sentences.en: How did Jeremy Thorpe end up as leader of the Liberal Party?
sentences.zh: 杰里米·索普是如何成为自由党领袖的？

sentences.en: Because he should probably have been a Tory, shouldn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他本该是个保守党人，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, he came from a Tory family.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他来自一个保守党家庭。

sentences.en: And this is actually a really interesting story about liberalism.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个关于自由主义的非常有趣的故事。

sentences.en: So liberalism had been the sort of governing creed of Britain for much of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 自由主义在19世纪的大部分时间里是英国的统治信条。

sentences.en: And it was the creed that Britain took into the First World War.
sentences.zh: 这也是英国带入第一次世界大战的信条。

sentences.en: And then liberalism really falls from grace.
sentences.zh: 然后自由主义真的失宠了。

sentences.en: And no ambitious politician will join the Liberal Party.
sentences.zh: 没有雄心勃勃的政治家会加入自由党。

sentences.en: I mean, you'll join the Labour Party or the Tories.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你会加入工党或保守党。

sentences.en: But the Liberal Party kind of lives on in Britain.
sentences.zh: 但自由党在英国以某种方式存活了下来。

sentences.en: I mean, that's one of the interesting stories about British politics in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是关于20世纪英国政治的有趣故事之一。

sentences.en: That, you know, we now have a Liberal Democrat Party and the liberal tradition never disappeared.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们现在有了自由民主党，自由主义传统从未消失。

sentences.en: And it sort of survived on what you call, I mean, not being rude, but there's kind of fringes, the geographical fringes.
sentences.zh: 它以某种方式在所谓的——我不是没礼貌——边缘地带生存了下来，地理上的边缘地带。

sentences.en: So North Wales, Scotland, and particularly in the southwest, in Cornwall and Devon.
sentences.zh: 比如北威尔士、苏格兰，特别是西南部，在康沃尔和德文郡。

sentences.en: And these are places with a big kind of Methodist tradition.
sentences.zh: 这些地方有着深厚的卫理公会传统。

sentences.en: So they're sort of dissenting kind of places.
sentences.zh: 所以它们是某种持不同政见的地方。

sentences.en: They're a long way from London.
sentences.zh: 它们离伦敦很远。

sentences.en: And serious places.
sentences.zh: 而且是严肃的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: If you're an earnest person, there's no real big trade union movement there.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个认真的人，那里没有真正的大型工会运动。

sentences.en: So you don't join the Labour Party if you're a sort of self-improving, sort of working class autodidact or something, or somebody who goes to chapel and really takes it seriously.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是一个自我提升的工人阶级自学者，或者是一个去教堂并非常认真对待它的人，你不会加入工党。

sentences.en: You join the Liberal Party.
sentences.zh: 你会加入自由党。

sentences.en: And you wear socks for sandals as a stereotype.
sentences.zh: 而且刻板印象中你会穿凉鞋配袜子。

sentences.en: Well, that is the stereotype, that you're kind of very well-meaning and you think a lot about the plight of the poor in foreign lands and that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是刻板印象，你非常善意，并且非常关心外国穷人的困境等等。

sentences.en: Now, Jeremy Thorpe is this consummate bounder.
sentences.zh: 现在，杰里米·索普是一个彻头彻尾的无赖。

sentences.en: I mean, he is the bounder's bounder.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是无赖中的无赖。

sentences.en: You know, he's at Eton, his one big thing was he played the violin.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他在伊顿时，他唯一的大事就是拉小提琴。

sentences.en: Then he goes to Oxford and he throws himself into the world of Oxford politics.
sentences.zh: 然后他去了牛津，投身于牛津政治的世界。

sentences.en: He becomes president of the Oxford Law Society, becomes president of the Oxford Union, which is a sort of classic staging post for ambitious politicians.
sentences.zh: 他成为牛津法律协会主席，成为牛津联盟主席，这是雄心勃勃的政治家们的经典跳板。

sentences.en: But he doesn't get involved with the Tory party, which you would expect.
sentences.zh: 但他没有加入你所预期的保守党。

sentences.en: He's drawn.
sentences.zh: 他被吸引了。

sentences.en: And I wonder whether even at this stage there's this sort of.
sentences.zh: 我怀疑即使在这个阶段，也有这种……

sentences.en: Thorpe is incredibly flamboyant and he's clearly gay.
sentences.zh: 索普非常浮夸，而且他显然是同性恋。

sentences.en: He knows he's gay, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他知道自己是同性恋。

sentences.en: So there's a question from, well, it's not even a question, it's a comment from Loose Morals.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个来自——嗯，这甚至不是一个问题，这是一个来自“松散道德”（Loose Morals）的评论。

sentences.en: All I remember about Jeremy Thorpe was his bad taste in hats.
sentences.zh: 关于杰里米·索普，我只记得他糟糕的帽子品味。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he wears a hat after everybody else no longer wears a hat.
sentences.zh: 是的，当别人都不再戴帽子时，他还在戴。

sentences.en: He wears a hat at a point where a hat is a sort of mark of eccentricity.
sentences.zh: 他在帽子成为一种古怪标志的时候戴帽子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think he went into the Liberal Party because if you were very talented, he's very funny, he's very clever, he's a barrister.
sentences.zh: 我认为他加入自由党是因为如果你非常有才华——他非常风趣，非常聪明，是个大律师。

sentences.en: Brilliant mimic.
sentences.zh: 出色的模仿者。

sentences.en: He's a brilliant mimic, exactly.
sentences.zh: 他是个出色的模仿者，没错。

sentences.en: So if you can do all those things, you know, there are 10 a penny in the Tory party, sort of posh, bounder types.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能做到所有这些，你知道，在保守党里，这种时髦的无赖类型多得是。

sentences.en: Whereas if you go into the Liberal Party, where basically it's incredibly staid and downbeat, you know, you can be leader of the Liberal Party.
sentences.zh: 而如果你加入自由党，那里基本上非常沉闷和低调，你知道，你可以成为自由党领袖。

sentences.en: You can become your personal vehicle.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它变成你的个人工具。

sentences.en: And I think there's an element of Thorpe knowing that, you know, it's almost an easy ride.
sentences.zh: 我认为索普有这种认识，你知道，这几乎是一条轻松的道路。

sentences.en: He can go and join.
sentences.zh: 他可以去加入。

sentences.en: I mean, all of that said, Tom, before we set Thorpe up as this kind of comic figure.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，话虽如此，汤姆，在我们把索普塑造成这种喜剧人物之前。

sentences.en: He's also genuinely liberal.
sentences.zh: 他也是一个真正的自由主义者。

sentences.en: And he's very hostile to apartheid, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 而且他非常敌视种族隔离，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he's a committed opponent of the apartheid regime in South Africa.
sentences.zh: 所以他是南非种族隔离政权的坚定反对者。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And actually that's going to run through this whole story, the South African connection.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这将贯穿整个故事，即南非的联系。

sentences.en: So he enters British politics in the 50s, really.
sentences.zh: 所以他是在50年代真正进入英国政治的。

sentences.en: And from that point onwards, you know, being very anti-racist, being very anti-apartheid, being very kind of progressive on these kinds of issues really marks you out in politics.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，你知道，非常反种族主义，非常反种族隔离，在这些问题上非常进步，确实让你在政治上与众不同。

sentences.en: Because it's not really that usual in, I mean, there are people in the Labour Party and there are some tourists.
sentences.zh: 因为这并不常见，我的意思是，工党里有这样的人，也有一些保守党人。

sentences.en: And especially not when combined with a penchant for wearing hats.
sentences.zh: 尤其是当它与戴帽子的嗜好结合在一起时，就更不寻常了。

sentences.en: Not if you're flamboyant.
sentences.zh: 如果你很浮夸的话，就不是这样了。

sentences.en: That's the weird thing.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: Being flamboyant in British politics often means you're very right wing.
sentences.zh: 在英国政治中，浮夸通常意味着你是极右翼。

sentences.en: Thorpe is not like that.
sentences.zh: 索普不是那样的人。

sentences.en: He's absolutely committed to human rights and to these kinds of issues that get him big ticks from the sort of socks and sandals people.
sentences.zh: 他绝对致力于人权和这些能让他从那些“凉鞋配袜子”的人那里获得好评的问题。

sentences.en: But he's funny.
sentences.zh: 但他很有趣。

sentences.en: He's very funny.
sentences.zh: 他非常有趣。

sentences.en: Here's a question.
sentences.zh: 这里有个问题。

sentences.en: So he's committed to human rights.
sentences.zh: 所以他致力于人权。

sentences.en: He's anti-raciSt.
sentences.zh: 他反种族主义。

sentences.en: Was he also committed to gay rights?
sentences.zh: 他也致力于同性恋权利吗？

sentences.en: And so is his homosexuality?
sentences.zh: 那么他的同性恋身份呢？

sentences.en: He's gay.
sentences.zh: 他是同性恋。

sentences.en: But he's flamboyantly gay at a time where it's illegal.
sentences.zh: 但在一个同性恋非法的时代，他是一个浮夸的同性恋。

sentences.en: So he's constantly skirting the edge of danger.

sentences.zh: 总之，他认为BOSS在密谋对付他。

sentences.en: And so Harold Wilson is saying to his cabinet ministers, you're hearing all these rumours about Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 所以哈罗德·威尔逊对他的内阁大臣们说，你们听到的关于索普的所有传言，

sentences.en: They're all created by BOSS.
sentences.zh: 都是BOSS制造出来的。

sentences.en: BOSS are involved with this.
sentences.zh: BOSS参与了这件事。

sentences.en: And BOSS do, in fact, know about it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，BOSS确实知道这件事。

sentences.en: They hate Thorpe because he's been campaigning against apartheid.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌索普，因为他一直在开展反种族隔离运动。

sentences.en: But they haven't created this story.
sentences.zh: 但他们并没有编造这个故事。

sentences.en: They've just sort of picked it up and are delighted by it and hoping to use it against him.
sentences.zh: 他们只是恰好发现了它，并对此感到高兴，希望能利用它来对付他。

sentences.en: So the way it starts to look more...
sentences.zh: 所以事情开始变得……

sentences.en: The way people start to believe the Thorpe story is that Scott starts to give his letters to the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 人们开始相信索普的故事，是因为斯科特开始把他的信件交给报社。

sentences.en: He's got this cache of letters, you see.
sentences.zh: 你瞧，他手里有一批信件。

sentences.en: That's one of the big things.
sentences.zh: 这是关键点之一。

sentences.en: He's got the letters that show that he and Thorpe did have a relationship.
sentences.zh: 他手里的信件证明了他和索普确实有过一段关系。

sentences.en: But also Thorpe's old crony, Peter Bessel, who's moved to California, he starts talking to the newspapers as well.
sentences.zh: 而且索普的老密友彼得·贝塞尔，那个搬到加州去的人，也开始向报社爆料。

sentences.en: So now you've got a feeding frenzy, a Fleet Street feeding frenzy, as the newspapers are competing for ever more lurid allegations.
sentences.zh: 现在这成了一场媒体狂欢，舰队街的媒体狂欢，报纸为了争夺更耸人听闻的指控而竞相报道。

sentences.en: And one of the things that makes this story very hard to assess is we don't know,
sentences.zh: 这个故事最难评估的一点在于，我们不知道，

sentences.en: and we'll never know how much some of these anecdotes have been concocted by the people telling them to sell papers.
sentences.zh: 而且永远也不会知道，这些轶事中有多少是为了卖报纸而被当事人编造出来的。

sentences.en: For example, the line, it's no better than shooting a sick dog.
sentences.zh: 比如那句“这跟射杀一条病狗没什么两样”。

sentences.en: I think Bessel made that up because it was such a great line.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是贝塞尔编的，因为这句话太精彩了。

sentences.en: And he could, you know, the Telegraph or the Mail or whoever it was would run with it.
sentences.zh: 他知道《每日电讯报》或《每日邮报》之类的报纸肯定会大肆报道。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's a kind of intriguing reminder of the pre-internet era that it takes this long to spill out.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，这提醒了我们互联网时代之前的情况，事情发酵需要这么久。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 确实是这样。

sentences.en: Now it would all be out in a couple of hours, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 要是现在，几个小时内全都会曝光，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, so it does take a very, you're right, it takes a very long time.
sentences.zh: 是啊，确实需要很长时间，你说得对。

sentences.en: So the sort of attempted murder is the autumn of 1975.
sentences.zh: 所以那次谋杀未遂发生在1975年秋天。

sentences.en: But then it's not till May 1976 that Thorpe steps down as leader of the Liberal Party, because the Sunday Times had printed some of his letters to Norman Scott.
sentences.zh: 但直到1976年5月，索普才辞去自由党领袖职务，因为《星期日泰晤士报》刊登了他写给诺曼·斯科特的一些信件。

sentences.en: And then the case rumbles on for a few more years.
sentences.zh: 之后这个案子又拖了好几年。

sentences.en: And there's kind of revelation after revelation, this slow drip, drip, drip in the newspapers.
sentences.zh: 报纸上不断爆出新的猛料，像滴水一样一点点渗透。

sentences.en: And the other thing that I should have mentioned is that one of the key people in pushing the story,
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我应该提一下，推动这个故事的关键人物之一，

sentences.en: who's another great character who actually didn't really appear so much, I think, in a very English scandal, is the satirist, Orberon Waugh.
sentences.zh: 也是另一个伟大的角色，虽然我觉得他在《英式丑闻》里出现得不多，那就是讽刺作家奥伯伦·沃。

sentences.en: So he's Evelyn Waugh's son, the son of the Brideshead revisited noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 他是伊夫林·沃的儿子，也就是《故园风雨后》作者的儿子。

sentences.en: He lives down in the West Country, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他住在西南部，对吧？

sentences.en: He lives in the West Country.
sentences.zh: 他住在西南部。

sentences.en: He knows of Thorpe, and he writes a diary for Private Eye magazine, in which he makes stuff up.
sentences.zh: 他认识索普，并为《私家侦探》杂志写日记，在里面编造各种事情。

sentences.en: So he writes this incredibly reactionary diary, in which he sort of says,
sentences.zh: 他写了一篇极其反动的日记，在里面他说，

sentences.zh: “昨晚我和玛格丽特公主共进晚餐，我们一致认为所有罢工者都应该当场枪毙”，或者类似的话。

sentences.en: But in the course of his diary of the 70s, he has a real vendetta against Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 但在他70年代的日记中，他确实对索普怀有深仇大恨。

sentences.en: I mean, he just calls himself a vendetta.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他自己就称之为“复仇”。

sentences.en: He says Thorpe is a hypocrite and a liar.
sentences.zh: 他说索普是个伪君子和骗子。

sentences.en: He has disgusting and revolting personal habits.
sentences.zh: 他有令人作呕和反感的个人习惯。

sentences.en: And he's particularly upset about the killing of Rinker.
sentences.zh: 而且他对杀害林克这件事特别愤怒。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when he hears about the dog, he says, this just confirms everything I've ever suspected about Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 所以当他听说那条狗的事时，他说，这证实了我对索普的所有怀疑。

sentences.en: Thorpe is a dog murderer.
sentences.zh: 索普是个杀狗凶手。

sentences.en: And really, I mean, in England, there could be no worse accusation than a dog murderer.
sentences.zh: 说真的，在英国，没有比“杀狗凶手”更糟糕的指控了。

sentences.en: The killing of the dog, rather than...
sentences.zh: 杀狗这件事，而不是……

sentences.zh: 如果被谋杀的是斯科特，那故事反而没那么精彩。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a better story because it's the dog, Rinker, the innocent dog, who is killed.
sentences.zh: 正是因为被杀的是林克，那条无辜的狗，这个故事才更引人入胜。

sentences.en: So before all this time, the sort of Crown Prosecution Service or whatever they were in the 70s are sort of amassing information.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之前，皇家检察署或者70年代叫什么名字的机构，一直在收集信息。

sentences.en: They decide they are going to charge Thorpe, Holmes, the fruit machine man, George Deacon, the carpet salesman, LeMessurier, the airline pilot, Newton.
sentences.zh: 他们决定起诉索普、霍姆斯、那个水果机商、地毯推销员乔治·迪肯、航空公司飞行员勒梅西耶，以及牛顿。

sentences.en: They're going to charge them all with conspiracy to murder.
sentences.zh: 他们要以共谋谋杀罪起诉所有人。

sentences.en: But that doesn't happen until after the next general election, the 1979 general election.
sentences.zh: 但这直到下一次大选，即1979年大选之后才发生。

sentences.en: So that gives Orber on War, the satirist, the chance to stand against Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 这给了讽刺作家奥伯伦·沃一个机会去竞选对抗索普。

sentences.en: Running for the dog party.
sentences.zh: 代表“狗狗党”参选。

sentences.en: Yeah, the dog lovers party.
sentences.zh: 是的，爱狗人士党。

sentences.en: Dog lovers party with its slogan, a better deal for your dog.
sentences.zh: 爱狗人士党，口号是“为你的狗争取更好的待遇”。

sentences.en: A better deal for your dog.
sentences.zh: 为你的狗争取更好的待遇。

sentences.en: So his election manifesto was suppressed by law because the judge said it would be prejudicial to the trial.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选宣言被法律禁止了，因为法官说这会影响审判的公正性。

sentences.en: Because Orber on War was campaigning for dogs and against Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 因为奥伯伦·沃是在为狗奔走，并反对索普。

sentences.en: He said dogs had had a very bad deal in Britain.
sentences.zh: 他说狗在英国受到了很不公平的待遇。

sentences.en: Thorpe wouldn't be going around killing them.
sentences.zh: 索普不应该到处杀狗。

sentences.en: And the judge wouldn't let him publish.
sentences.zh: 法官不让他发表。

sentences.en: So he won 79 votes, War.
sentences.zh: 所以沃只赢得了79张选票。

sentences.en: And Thorpe loses, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 而索普输了，对吧？

sentences.en: But actually by a surprisingly small amount, considering...
sentences.zh: 但考虑到……其实输得并不多。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's tons of support for Thorpe in his local manor, as it were.
sentences.zh: 是的，索普在他的选区里还是有大量支持者的。

sentences.en: And so on the theme of change in attitudes to homosexuality, lots of voters don't seem to have worried about that at all.
sentences.zh: 所以关于对同性恋态度的转变，很多选民似乎根本不在乎这一点。

sentences.en: Well, Thorpe is married.
sentences.zh: 嗯，索普结婚了。

sentences.en: Thorpe has been twice married.
sentences.zh: 索普结过两次婚。

sentences.en: So a lot of people, I think, just didn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为很多人只是不相信这些事。

sentences.en: And it's that weird thing, Tom, where I think a lot of voters had formed an attachment to Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这是一种很奇怪的现象，我觉得很多选民对索普产生了感情。

sentences.en: And they just simply refused to believe that he could have been guilty of any of the things that he was accused of.
sentences.zh: 他们根本拒绝相信他会犯下任何被指控的罪行。

sentences.en: But he loses.
sentences.zh: 但他还是输了。

sentences.en: Yeah, but he does lose.
sentences.zh: 是的，他确实输了。

sentences.en: He loses.
sentences.zh: 他输了。

sentences.en: And then after the election, which sees Mrs. Thatcher come to power, Thorpe comes to trial with the three other conspirators in the High Court.
sentences.zh: 大选后，撒切尔夫人上台，索普和其他三名共谋者在高等法院受审。

sentences.en: Yes, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.zh: 在老贝利法院。

sentences.en: In the Old Bailey.
sentences.zh: 在老贝利法院。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, OK, so because this is another aspect of Britain that has vanished completely, is the tradition of the comically reactionary, out-of-touch judge.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是英国另一个已经彻底消失的方面，那就是那种滑稽、反动且脱离现实的法官传统。

sentences.en: Yeah, Lord Justice Cantley, was it?
sentences.zh: 是的，是坎特利大法官，对吧？

sentences.en: Lord Justice Cantley, yeah.
sentences.zh: 坎特利大法官，没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Who basically presides over the case.
sentences.zh: 他基本上主持了整个案件。

sentences.zh: 他的总结陈词非常偏袒索普，以至于索普被判无罪。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Have you got it there, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你那里有记录吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: I haven't.
sentences.zh: 我没有。

sentences.en: But famously, it then gets parodied by Peter Cook, who's the, I mean, he's basically, he's the guy who funds Private Eye.
sentences.zh: 但众所周知，后来彼得·库克模仿了他，他基本上就是那个资助《私家侦探》的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Part of Dudley Moore and Peter Cook.
sentences.zh: 达德利·摩尔和彼得·库克组合的一员。

sentences.en: He was part of the Beyond the Fringe, kind of the great genius of British comedy.
sentences.zh: 他是《超越边缘》的一员，是英国喜剧界的天才。

sentences.en: And he does this kind of almost pitch-perfect parody.
sentences.zh: 他做了一段几乎完美的模仿。

sentences.en: Well, Cantley had described Scott.
sentences.zh: 嗯，坎特利曾这样描述斯科特。

sentences.en: He'd said in his summing up, he'd said, Mr. Thorpe, public servant of many years standing, Scott, scrounger, parasite, hypocrite, homosexual.
sentences.zh: 他在总结陈词中说，索普先生是多年来尽职尽责的公仆，而斯科特是乞丐、寄生虫、伪君子、同性恋。

sentences.en: And sort of, you know, he completely loaded the, and yeah, as you say, Peter Cook does this absolutely brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 他完全带偏了节奏，正如你所说，彼得·库克模仿得非常精彩。

sentences.en: Self-confessed player of the pink oboe, is the famous phrase.
sentences.zh: “自称吹奏粉红双簧管的人”，这是那句名言。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, basically what he does is, the reason that's so good is that he basically intersperses with what Cantley genuinely said.
sentences.zh: 是的，他之所以模仿得那么好，是因为他把坎特利真正说过的话穿插在里面。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think, I mean, that's, maybe that's one of the reasons why, maybe it's just middle age, that British comedy doesn't seem quite as funny these days.
sentences.zh: 我想，这也许就是为什么，或者仅仅是因为人到中年，觉得现在的英国喜剧没那么好笑了。

sentences.en: It's because judges aren't as funny.
sentences.zh: 是因为法官们没那么搞笑了。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's nothing to kick againSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，没什么可吐槽的了。

sentences.en: Establishment figures aren't as funny.
sentences.zh: 建制派人物没那么搞笑了。

sentences.en: Because back then, the establishment really was the establishment, and you could laugh at it.
sentences.zh: 因为那时候，建制派确实是建制派，你可以嘲笑他们。

sentences.en: Whereas now the establishment is all down with the kids.
sentences.zh: 而现在，建制派都跟年轻人打成一片了。

sentences.en: So they're not as instantly amusing.
sentences.zh: 所以他们没那么有趣了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so great for Jeremy Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 总之，这对杰里米·索普来说是件好事。

sentences.en: He gets acquitted, but his career...
sentences.zh: 他被判无罪，但他的职业生涯……

sentences.en: His career is juSt...
sentences.zh: 他的职业生涯简直……

sentences.zh: 汤姆，我认为他必须被判无罪，因为检方的证据几乎必然是非常薄弱的。

sentences.en: It's all based on hearsay.
sentences.zh: 全都是基于传闻。

sentences.zh: 好了，这是乔纳森·梅策尔给你的一个问题。

sentences.zh: 陪审团根据“排除合理怀疑”原则判决无罪，但审视当时和现在的所有证据，索普可能是有罪还是无罪的？

sentences.zh: 你怎么看？

sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为陪审团必须判他无罪，因为有一个细节……

sentences.zh: 好吧，那不是问题所在。

sentences.zh: 不，我只想说一件事。

sentences.zh: 那些关键的控方证人，后来发现根据他们与报社的协议，如果索普被定罪，他们能拿到更多的钱。

sentences.en: So, I mean, that obviously looks very...
sentences.zh: 所以，这看起来显然非常……

sentences.en: Okay, so they were always...
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以他们一直……

sentences.en: Okay, but that's not quite the question.
sentences.zh: 好吧，但那不是问题的重点。

sentences.en: So maybe he had to be a critic because there wasn't the evidence or because people had been tampering with the witnesses or whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以也许他必须被判无罪，因为证据不足，或者因为有人篡改了证词之类的。

sentences.zh: 但你认为索普是否真的策划了谋杀诺曼·斯科特的企图？

sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是的。

sentences.zh: 我觉得他可能并不是真的想那么做。

sentences.en: But I'll tell you what's really...
sentences.zh: 但我告诉你真正……

sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们还没提到那件最要命的事，这正好是我抛出一个心头好事实的机会。

sentences.en: Thorpe, it's the fact that he gets the money.
sentences.zh: 索普，事实就是他拿到了那笔钱。

sentences.zh: 他拿到了钱，从一个叫杰克·海伍德爵士的人那里筹集到的，那是一位住在巴哈马的英国百万富翁，也是自由党的捐赠人。

sentences.en: Now, some listeners...
sentences.zh: 现在，有些听众……

sentences.zh: 他是……的主席

sentences.zh: 更好的……

sentences.zh: 他在20世纪90年代成为了狼队足球俱乐部的老板。

sentences.zh: 而且汤姆，我觉得你其实能理解为什么索普……

sentences.zh: 我是说，你可以想象索普感到被困住了。

sentences.zh: 他过去有过一段关系，他觉得那种因性取向被曝光的恐惧让他永远无法摆脱。

sentences.zh: 他觉得他必须做点什么。

sentences.en: And whether he said it first as a joke, or whether he really meant it, I think when it's happening at so many removes, it probably never really seemed real to him.
sentences.zh: 不管他最初是开玩笑说的，还是真的这么想，我觉得当这件事经过这么多层转述时，对他来说可能从来没显得真实过。

sentences.en: Oh, just get rid of him.
sentences.zh: 哦，干掉他就行了。

sentences.en: I was 11, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时11岁。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was 11.
sentences.zh: 是的，我11岁。

sentences.en: And I had a vague sense of what was going on.
sentences.zh: 我对当时发生的事情有一种模糊的感觉。

sentences.en: And I wasn't entirely sure what Jeremy Thorpe exactly was supposed to have done.
sentences.zh: 我不完全确定杰里米·索普到底被指控做了什么。

sentences.en: But I kind of vaguely knew that it was something bad.
sentences.zh: 但我隐约知道那是一件坏事。

sentences.en: And we have a comment here from Tony McGowan, opening batsman in the authors, a little bit older than me, I should say.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有一条来自托尼·麦高文的评论，他是作者群里的开路先锋，我得说他比我稍微年长一点。

sentences.en: I hope you'll be mentioning the terrible jokes that went around every school in the wake of the scandal, e.g.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能提到丑闻发生后在每所学校流传的那些糟糕笑话，比如：

sentences.en: What happened when Jeremy Thorpe found Norman Scott stowing away on his yacht?
sentences.zh: 当杰里米·索普发现诺曼·斯科特偷渡在他的游艇上时发生了什么？

sentences.en: He made him work his passage.
sentences.zh: 他让他干活抵船费。

sentences.en: So there was...
sentences.zh: 所以当时……

sentences.en: The trial kind of provided grist for schoolboy jokes like that.
sentences.zh: 审判为这类校园笑话提供了素材。

sentences.en: And there was a kind of, you know, the tradition of British smut, of innuendo, of anti-gay jokes.
sentences.zh: 而且当时有一种英国式的下流传统，一种影射，一种反同性恋的笑话。

sentences.en: I mean, this kind of powered that particular mill.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这种氛围推动了那台特定的磨坊。

sentences.en: And then there's a very interesting comment from Pat Roberts.
sentences.zh: 然后还有一条来自帕特·罗伯茨的非常有趣的评论。

sentences.en: I first heard the word homosexual with regard to Thorpe.
sentences.zh: 我第一次听到“同性恋”这个词就是关于索普的。

sentences.en: I was about nine.
sentences.zh: 我当时大约九岁。

sentences.en: The word bimbo with regard to Gary Hart.
sentences.zh: 关于加里·哈特的“荡妇”一词。

sentences.en: And about a sexual practice I won't mention with regard to Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 还有关于比尔·克林顿的某种我不便提及的性行为。

sentences.en: Do political scandals give permission to the respectable media to talk dirty?
sentences.zh: 政治丑闻是否给了体面媒体谈论肮脏话题的许可？

sentences.en: So it basically gives permission to schoolchildren and to the media to deal in kind of smutty subjects that otherwise, perhaps, back in the late 70s,
sentences.zh: 所以它基本上给了小学生和媒体处理那种下流话题的许可，而在70年代末，

sentences.en: people were more restrained in talking about them, perhaps, than it would be now.
sentences.zh: 人们在谈论这些话题时可能比现在更克制。

sentences.en: I think the good example of that is the very existence of the News of the World newspaper, now defunct, which in the sort of 50s, 60s, 70s, you know, at the weekend, on Sundays,
sentences.zh: 我觉得一个很好的例子就是《世界新闻报》的存在，现在已经停刊了，在50、60、70年代，周末，周日的时候，

sentences.en: the News of the World always had stories about flandering vicars or, you know, people caught in compromising situations.
sentences.zh: 《世界新闻报》总是有关于偷情的牧师，或者被抓到处于尴尬境地的人的故事。

sentences.en: And you're right, it's a kind of prurience to it, but it was always an excuse to tell sort of titillating stories and stories about wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 你说得对，这有一种窥淫癖，但这总是讲述煽情故事和关于不端行为故事的借口。

sentences.en: And I think the Thorpe scandal was the consummate example of that.
sentences.zh: 我认为索普丑闻是这方面的典型例子。

sentences.en: But also, it's so, I think it really, why it really matters is because in the 1970s, there was a sense of decrepitude in British politics and a sense of establishment seediness.
sentences.zh: 但同样，我认为它真正重要的地方在于，在20世纪70年代，英国政坛有一种衰败感和建制派的肮脏感。

sentences.en: And this was precise, I mean, the big winner was Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 而这正是……我是说，最大的赢家是玛格丽特·撒切尔。

sentences.en: You know, unimpeachable private life, a woman, breath of, you know, sort of projected herself.
sentences.zh: 你知道，无可指责的私生活，一位女性，她展现出了一种……

sentences.en: It's the same thing as with the Perfume scandal in the early 60s.
sentences.zh: 这和60年代初的普罗富莫丑闻是一回事。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Put pay to the Macmillan government, gave it the kind of aura of shabbiness and decrepitude.
sentences.zh: 终结了麦克米伦政府，给它蒙上了一种破旧和衰败的氛围。

sentences.en: And Thorpe is a consensus politician.
sentences.zh: 而索普是一位共识型政治家。

sentences.en: He's a politician of that post-war sort of slightly social democratic consensus.
sentences.zh: 他是那种战后略带社会民主共识的政治家。

sentences.en: And that's what Margaret Thatcher in 1979, the year that he's tried, that's what she says she wants to smash.
sentences.zh: 而那正是玛格丽特·撒切尔在1979年，也就是他受审的那一年，声称想要粉碎的东西。

sentences.en: And it's very telling, you know, the Taurus had lost in 1974 because so many of their voters, something like two million of their voters had defected to the Liberals.
sentences.zh: 这非常能说明问题，保守党在1974年输了，因为他们太多的选民，大约两百万选民倒戈投向了自由党。

sentences.en: Those voters return in the year of the Thorpe trial to Margaret Thatcher.
sentences.zh: 那些选民在索普审判的那一年回到了玛格丽特·撒切尔身边。

sentences.en: And they give her the impetus that she needs to go and sort of change everything in the 1980s.
sentences.zh: 他们给了她所需的动力，让她去改变80年代的一切。

sentences.en: I mean, I thought what Hugh Grant's portrayal of Jeremy Thorpe powerfully conveyed was the charm and the wit and the kind of debonair qualities.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为休·格兰特对杰里米·索普的刻画有力地传达了他的魅力、机智和那种风度翩翩的特质。

sentences.en: And there's Ian Jones has given a transcript of an interview between Robin Day, the great inquisitor of the 70s and 80s,
sentences.zh: 伊恩·琼斯提供了一份罗宾·戴（70和80年代伟大的审问者）采访索普的文字记录，

sentences.en: interviewing Thorpe on losing his North Devon seat at the 1979 general election.
sentences.zh: 当时索普在1979年大选中失去了北德文郡的席位。

sentences.en: And Robin Day, Mr. Thorpe, do you think your prosecution for conspiracy to murder was a factor in your defeat?
sentences.zh: 罗宾·戴问：“索普先生，你认为你因密谋谋杀而受审是你失败的一个因素吗？”

sentences.en: To which Thorpe replies, put it like this, Robin, I don't think it helped.
sentences.zh: 索普回答说：“这么说吧，罗宾，我不认为这有什么帮助。”

sentences.en: Yeah, well, Thorpe was really funny.
sentences.zh: 是的，好吧，索普真的很幽默。

sentences.en: I mean, Thorpe would do a thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，索普会做一件事。

sentences.en: I'm obviously a very charismatic man.
sentences.zh: 我显然是个非常有魅力的人。

sentences.en: Thorpe would do a thing that you never see on political panel shows.
sentences.zh: 索普会做一件你在政治座谈节目中从没见过的事。

sentences.en: So he would appear on a panel show and then he would impersonate the other people.
sentences.zh: 他会出现在座谈节目上，然后模仿其他人。

sentences.en: We don't have enough politicians doing that.
sentences.zh: 我们没有足够的政治家这样做。

sentences.en: No, politicians don't do enough impersonations.
sentences.zh: 不，政治家们模仿得不够多。

sentences.en: OK, so I mean, I think that basically covers it because it didn't really have an enduring influence, an enduring impact.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是说，我认为这基本上涵盖了，因为它并没有产生持久的影响。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a kind of interesting waymark.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一种有趣的里程碑。

sentences.en: As you say, it kind of signals the end of a particular period in British politics and the beginning of a new one.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，它标志着英国政治一个特定时期的结束和新时期的开始。

sentences.en: It's also, as we said, an interesting waymark in the kind of evolution of attitudes to homosexuality.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，这也是在对待同性恋态度的演变中一个有趣的里程碑。

sentences.en: And of course, it's the most famous assassination of a dog in British history.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是英国历史上最著名的暗杀狗事件。

sentences.en: We had a lot of questions about dogs, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了很多关于狗的问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And since this was Ian Keeley's idea that we do these, I think we should, yeah, Paul Keeley, sorry.
sentences.zh: 既然这是伊恩·基利的提议，我想我们应该……是的，保罗·基利，抱歉。

sentences.en: I think we should end with a question that he's asked.
sentences.zh: 我想我们应该以他提出的一个问题结束。

sentences.en: And has the assassination of a dog, in this case, poor old Rinker, ever had such reverberations in public life?
sentences.zh: 暗杀一只狗（在本案中是可怜的老林克）在公共生活中产生过如此大的反响吗？

sentences.en: I haven't made a special study of dogs.
sentences.zh: 我没有专门研究过狗。

sentences.en: When I got that question, I threw my hands up and put it out.
sentences.zh: 当我收到那个问题时，我举手投降并把它发了出去。

sentences.en: And we've had a number of excellent replies.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了许多出色的回复。

sentences.en: So we've had one from Dunlin Temmink, who suggests Gellert, and that's a great story.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一条来自邓林·特明克的回复，他提到了盖勒特，那是一个伟大的故事。

sentences.en: Gellert was the hound of Llewellyn the Great in Wales, who came back to find his child's cradle had been turned over.
sentences.zh: 盖勒特是威尔士卢埃林大帝的猎犬，他回来发现孩子的摇篮被翻倒了。

sentences.en: The baby itself had vanished.
sentences.zh: 婴儿本身不见了。

sentences.en: And there was Gellert, his dog, with blood kind of dripping from its chops.
sentences.zh: 盖勒特，他的狗，嘴边滴着血。

sentences.en: And so Llewellyn assumes that Gellert has killed the baby.
sentences.zh: 于是卢埃林认为盖勒特杀了婴儿。

sentences.en: He kills the hound.
sentences.zh: 他杀死了猎犬。

sentences.en: The hound gives a kind of faithful, trusting yowl and then keels over.
sentences.zh: 猎犬发出一声忠诚、信任的哀鸣，然后倒下了。

sentences.en: And Llewellyn goes next door and finds the baby well and alive and a dead wolf that Gellert has killed.
sentences.zh: 卢埃林走进隔壁，发现婴儿安然无恙，还有一只被盖勒特杀死的死狼。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's a good story.
sentences.zh: 那是个好故事。

sentences.en: It survived the assassination of Lincoln himself.
sentences.zh: 它甚至在林肯本人的暗杀事件中幸存了下来。

sentences.en: Very boring.
sentences.zh: 真无聊。

sentences.en: And then he got assassinated by a drunk shortly after Lincoln's funeral.
sentences.zh: 然后在林肯葬礼后不久，它被一个醉汉暗杀了。

sentences.en: Assassinated?
sentences.zh: 暗杀？

sentences.en: Can you assassinate?
sentences.zh: 可以暗杀吗？

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: If it's Lincoln's dog, you can assassinate.
sentences.zh: 如果是林肯的狗，你就可以暗杀。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Dave Walters, the story, I think, actually, which we've touched on before, a stray dog did cause a war.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·沃尔特斯的故事，我想，其实我们之前提到过，一只流浪狗确实引发了一场战争。

sentences.en: The War of the Stray Dog was a Greek-Bulgarian crisis in 1925,
sentences.zh: “流浪狗战争”是1925年的一场希腊-保加利亚危机，

sentences.en: which resulted in a brief invasion of Bulgaria by Greece near the border town of Petritch after the killing of a Greek captain, chasing the dog and a sentry by Bulgarian soldiers.
sentences.zh: 起因是一名希腊上尉在追赶狗时被保加利亚士兵射杀，导致希腊短暂入侵了边境城镇佩特里奇。

sentences.en: And then we have called Dubs, Sir Richard Sharples was assassinated in 1973 in Bermuda, along with his ADC, Hugh Sayers, and his dog, Horser.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还有卡尔·杜布斯提到的，理查德·夏普尔斯爵士于1973年在百慕大被暗杀，连同他的副官休·塞耶斯和他的狗霍瑟一起。

sentences.en: So there are some famous dogs.
sentences.zh: 所以确实有一些著名的狗。

sentences.en: I think we should end.
sentences.zh: 我想我们该结束了。

sentences.en: I don't know about dead dogs, but I know about a lost dog that was important.
sentences.zh: 我不知道死狗的事，但我知道一只很重要的走失狗。

sentences.en: It's both a nod back to a previous podcast and anticipating a future podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 这既是对之前播客的致意，也是对未来播客的预告。

sentences.en: So the late Adolf Hitler had a dog when he was in the trenches in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 已故的阿道夫·希特勒在第一次世界大战的战壕里时有一只狗。

sentences.en: And he was friendlier with the dog than with any of the fellows in his sort of platoon or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他和那只狗比和他排里的任何战友都要亲近。

sentences.en: And he became very close to this dog.
sentences.zh: 他变得和这只狗非常亲密。

sentences.en: And eventually they were told to move down the line.
sentences.zh: 最终他们被告知要沿着战线转移。

sentences.en: And the dog had gone off for a walk or something, and Hitler couldn't find it.
sentences.zh: 那只狗出去散步了还是怎么的，希特勒找不到它。

sentences.en: And they moved out, and he never saw the dog again.
sentences.zh: 他们出发了，他再也没见过那只狗。

sentences.en: And his comrades said they never saw him as upset as he was after the loss of that dog.
sentences.zh: 他的战友们说，他们从未见过他像失去那只狗后那样难过。

sentences.en: Now, the reason I say it's a nod to a future podcast is when I was writing my children's history of the Second World War, in the first chapter I introduced Hitler as a character.
sentences.zh: 现在，我之所以说这是对未来播客的致意，是因为我在写我的儿童版二战史时，在第一章我把希特勒作为角色引入。

sentences.en: And I had this stuff about Hitler and the dog, and I had written it in a very tear-jerking way.
sentences.zh: 我写了关于希特勒和狗的内容，写得非常催泪。

sentences.en: And at this point I hadn't – I don't think I'd said that Hitler was going to be the baddie or something.
sentences.zh: 当时我还没有——我想我还没说希特勒会是个坏蛋之类的。

sentences.en: And my son read it.
sentences.zh: 我儿子读了它。

sentences.en: And when he saw the stuff about the dog – I mean, he didn't care about the deaths of all these people in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 当他看到关于狗的内容时——我是说，他根本不在乎一战中所有这些人的死亡。

sentences.en: But when he read about the dog going missing, he was sort of lip-quivered.
sentences.zh: 但当他读到狗失踪时，他嘴唇颤抖了。

sentences.en: And then he said to me, is the person with the dog Hitler?
sentences.zh: 然后他问我，那个有狗的人是希特勒吗？

sentences.en: And I said, yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，是他。

sentences.en: And he said, oh, well, you can't have the dog.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，那你不能有那只狗。

sentences.en: Because any child reading this book will think that the lost dog, that must be the hero.
sentences.zh: 因为任何读这本书的孩子都会认为那只走失的狗一定是英雄。

sentences.en: And so I had to take the dog out.
sentences.zh: 所以我不得不把狗删掉。

sentences.en: I had to cut it.
sentences.zh: 我不得不把它剪掉。

sentences.en: I had to cut it completely.
sentences.zh: 我不得不完全剪掉它。

sentences.en: Because no villain would ever have a dog in a children's book.
sentences.zh: 因为在儿童读物里，反派绝不可能有狗。

sentences.en: I mean, so we're going to be recording an episode next week on children's history.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们下周要录制一期关于儿童历史的节目。

sentences.en: And I think we've been talking about dogs.
sentences.zh: 我想我们一直在谈论狗。

sentences.en: We've been talking about children's history.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在谈论儿童历史。

sentences.en: And we've also been talking about the contribution of our listeners.
sentences.zh: 我们也一直在谈论听众的贡献。

sentences.en: And I'd like to just fade out by a wonderful conversation that our Magna Carta episode inspired.
sentences.zh: 我想以我们大宪章那一集所激发的一段精彩对话来收尾。

sentences.en: So we had some criticism from Dano about that.
sentences.zh: 我们收到了一些来自达诺的批评。

sentences.en: A bit of a rant after listening to the Magna Carta episode of the rest of the history the other day.
sentences.zh: 前几天听完《历史余谈》的大宪章那一集后，他发了一通牢骚。

sentences.en: Feel free to argue with me.
sentences.zh: 欢迎随时反驳我。

sentences.en: I will not defend John.
sentences.zh: 我不会为约翰辩护。

sentences.en: He was a bad king.
sentences.zh: 他是个坏国王。

sentences.en: And by the sound of it, a bad person.
sentences.zh: 听起来，还是个坏人。

sentences.en: But, and so Dano goes on with his thread.
sentences.zh: 但是，达诺继续了他的讨论。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But we then have a comment from Goalie X, who says, what about the fact that his chief advisor was a snake?
sentences.zh: 但我们随后收到了一条来自Goalie X的评论，他说，他的首席顾问是一条蛇，这怎么说？

sentences.en: To which Dano, you know, huge credit to Dano.
sentences.zh: 对此达诺，你知道，非常佩服达诺。

sentences.en: He says, OK, that I will grant you is a bad look.
sentences.zh: 他说，好吧，这一点我承认确实很难看。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think that that's the measure of the people who are listening to us, is that they can disagree, but they do it amicably.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是我们听众的水平，他们可以有分歧，但他们能友好地交流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If you don't believe King John's advisor was a snake, just Google it.
sentences.zh: 如果你不相信约翰王的顾问是一条蛇，去谷歌搜一下就知道了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: So I think on that note, Dominic, thank you for a tour de force, a brilliant explication of the Jeremy Thorpe scandal.
sentences.zh: 所以我想借此机会，多米尼克，感谢你带来这场精彩绝伦的讲述，对杰里米·索普丑闻进行了极其出色的剖析。

sentences.en: Thank you to Paul Keely for suggesting it.
sentences.zh: 感谢保罗·基利提出的建议。

sentences.en: And I hope that our, those listeners who'd never heard of the Jeremy Thorpe scandal will feel that it was well worth doing an episode on.
sentences.zh: 我也希望那些此前从未听说过杰里米·索普丑闻的听众，会觉得做这一期节目是非常值得的。

sentences.en: So we will speak to you soon.
sentences.zh: 那么我们很快再见。

sentences.en: Thanks very much for listening.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
